title: DiFA: Inference-Time Forward-Process Alignment for Diffusion Models
claim: Standard samplers use each prediction once in open loop; ours feeds predictions through a running consensus to refine them before solving.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right, dashed divider, feedback loop with consensus ellipse
description: The figure has two horizontal rows separated by a dashed gray line. The top row shows the standard sampler: x_t goes into a gray 'Standard Denoiser' box, then a gray 'Numerical Solver (Open-Loop)' box, then out to x_{t-1}. The bottom row, titled 'Forward-Aligned Prediction (DiFA View)' in bold blue, is the proposed method. A blue 'Current Prediction' box sends an 'observation' arrow to a small black brain-like fusion icon. An orange 'Temporal Consensus' ellipse sits above it. It has a self-loop labeled 'Sequential Attention' and sends a 'consensus' arrow down into the icon. A dashed gray 'update' arrow runs from the current prediction back to the consensus. A pink 'deviation r_t' arrow leads to a blue 'DiFA-refined Prediction' box, then a gray 'Downstream Solver' box, then x_{t-1}. The refinement equation sits above the refined box. The eye goes first to the colorful bottom row.
caption: DiFA Mechanism of Inference-Time Forward-Process Alignment. Traditional samplers (Top) use each denoiser prediction only for the current solver step, discarding temporal redundancy along the trajectory. DiFA (Bottom) constructs a forward-aligned temporal consensus ˆxcons 0 (t) = ˆx(t)
abstract: The prevailing inference framework for diffusion models formulates generation fundamentally as a problem of numerical integration. This perspective casts the model as an exact estimator, neglecting the inherent statistical uncertainty of the denoising process. In this work, we propose Forward-Process Aligned Diffusion prediction (\textbf{DiFA}), a training-free framework that reframes inference-time data prediction refinement as a sequential state estimation problem. Rather than reusing past outputs solely for numerical integration, DiFA treats iterative data predictions along the reverse trajectory as correlated observations to build a forward-aligned temporal consensus. Inspired by Kalman filtering, this consensus aggregates historical predictions according to structural consistency and noise-level compatibility. To counteract the over-smoothing tendency of temporal consensus, we introduce a deviation guidance mechanism to adaptively preserve residual details. Empirically, DiFA yields significant improvements on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet across the evaluated metrics, including FID, IS, and FD-DINOv2, demonstrating that aligning inference with the forward statistical structure substantially improves generative fidelity.
